author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Concord public-safety crews responded to a cluster of unrelated incidents Thursday afternoon, stretching resources across the city and nearby highways. Around 2:15 p.m., smoke reported near Interstate 393’s Exit 1 led state police to a campsite where people were burning trash. Authorities addressed the fire without reporting injuries.

Minutes later, a truck towing a camper lost its fuel pump near Intervale and Fort Eddy roads. An estimated 25 to 30 gallons of gasoline spilled, requiring firefighters and other crews to contain and clean the scene. The location sits near a busy commercial area and highway approaches, making traffic control part of the response.

Emergency personnel also went to a two-vehicle crash near Interstate 93’s Exit 14 involving a Toyota driven by a Chichester resident and a Nissan driven by an Antrim resident. No injuries were apparent, but both vehicles needed towing. Additional alarm calls followed later in the afternoon. The sequence illustrates how routine incidents can overlap quickly, requiring coordination among city firefighters, Concord police and New Hampshire State Police.
dek: Firefighters, police and state troopers handled several overlapping Thursday-afternoon calls, including a gasoline spill and a two-vehicle interstate crash.
headline: Concord crews juggle camp fire, fuel spill and I-93 crash
